
## 2026-09-05 — Backfill: Phase 7 setup is additive and safe for existing profiles
**Phase:** 7
**Decision:** First run is a five-step setup for name/units, sessions-per-week, active
program, optional starting working weights, and non-workout activity cadence. Every step
has a default. Re-running setup from Settings edits configuration without deleting logged
history. Only profiles created by Phase 7 explicitly carry `setupComplete: false`; an older
profile with no such field is treated as already configured and never forced into setup by
an update. Starting weights prefill a first performance only; real logged history outranks
them afterward.
**Reasoning:** Phase 7 had landed in code and tests without an architectural entry in this
log. The compatibility rule is load-bearing: onboarding must never turn a software update
into a migration ceremony for an existing user, and configuration must not manufacture
training history.
**Confidence:** specified by the shipped Phase 7 behavior and docs/07 acceptance criteria.
**Needs Cory:** no

## 2026-09-05 — Backfill: activitySchedule owns cadence and supersedes attribute sections
**Phase:** 7 / cadence model
**Decision:** Non-workout activities have one profile-owned cadence: OFF, DAILY, or X/week
(1–7). `activitySchedule` is authoritative; `dailyActivityIds` remains only as a backwards-
compatible mirror. Weekly completion counts distinct logged calendar days, not taps. Today
is organized by time horizon — DAILY then THIS WEEK — rather than the older TRAIN /
RECOVER / SHARPEN attribute-family grouping. OFF activities remain one control away and
score identically when logged. The DAILY section is the immediate one-view surface; THIS
WEEK deliberately scrolls below it.
**Reasoning:** Cadence answers the user's operational question — when does this belong —
while attribute colour already answers what RPG stat it feeds. Keeping both as top-level
section systems duplicated information and made the one-view rule impossible on larger
program days. Distinct-day counting prevents repeated taps from satisfying a weekly habit.
Placement must never become a reward multiplier or a punishment mechanism.
**Confidence:** specified by the cadence rebuild and Cory's explicit one-view ruling.
**Needs Cory:** no

## 2026-09-05 — Backfill: Phase 8 hardens the existing product instead of adding systems
**Phase:** 8
**Decision:** Phase 8 is a polish/hardening pass only. It adds recoverable startup/screen /
workout/battle errors, accessible empty states and live regions, rem-based dynamic type,
visible focus, 44px targets, iOS input-zoom protection, reduced-motion/contrast/forced-
colors/transparency handling, dual Node 22/24 CI, syntax checks, and long-horizon cadence /
XP stress regressions. It does not alter XP philosophy, cadence semantics, program logic or
battle rewards.
**Reasoning:** Polish is safest when it can be falsified without moving the product model.
The stress tests exist specifically to prove that accessibility and surface changes do not
quietly reintroduce punishment, XP subtraction, cadence debt, persistence loss or runtime-
version drift.
**Confidence:** specified by docs/07 Phase 8 and the Phase 8 regression suite.
**Needs Cory:** no
